legend: You are given a permutation p$$$p$$$ of [1,2,…n]$$$[1, 2, \ldots n]$$$ (n$$$n$$$ is even).
You can perform the following operation:

Select a subsequence †$$$^\dagger$$$ (say t$$$t$$$) of length 2k$$$2k$$$ (k$$$k$$$ does not need to be the same across operations) such that max(t1,t2,…,tk)<min(tk+1,tk+2,…,t2k)$$$\max(t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_k)  \lt  \min(t_{k+1}, t_{k+2}, \ldots, t_{2k})$$$ or min(t1,t2,…,tk)>max(tk+1,tk+2,…,t2k)$$$\min(t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_k)  \gt  \max(t_{k+1}, t_{k+2}, \ldots, t_{2k})$$$. Remove t$$$t$$$ from p$$$p$$$.
You want to make p$$$p$$$ empty using the minimum number of operations.
You must also print the subsequence used in each operation, printing the values (not the indices).

†$$$^\dagger$$$ A sequence x$$$x$$$ is a subsequence of a sequence y$$$y$$$ if x$$$x$$$ can be obtained from y$$$y$$$ by deleting several (possibly, zero or all) elements. For example, [1,3]$$$[1, 3]$$$, [1,2,3]$$$[1, 2, 3]$$$, and [2,3]$$$[2, 3]$$$ are subsequences of [1,2,3]$$$[1, 2, 3]$$$. On the other hand, [3,1]$$$[3, 1]$$$ and [2,1,3]$$$[2, 1, 3]$$$ are not subsequences of [1,2,3]$$$[1, 2, 3]$$$.

note: In the first test case, we can select t=p$$$t = p$$$ and make p$$$p$$$ empty in one operation.
